correctness.rationale: For V=C^6 with nondegenerate bivector pi, the Koszul evaluation quotient yields exact vector-bundle sequence 0->E(-1)->Omega^2_{P5}(2)->O->0: the map is surjective since a five-dimensional subspace cannot be isotropic in symplectic dimension six. On any smooth twisted cubic C in P(U)=P3, Ann(U)=A has dimension two and the middle term is O_C(-2)^3 + O_C(-1)^6 + O_C. The last O maps by pi|Lambda^2 A. If nonzero, split off O and get E|C=O(2)^6 + O(1)^3. If zero, the cross term O(-1)^6 -> O has no basepoint because pi-sharp(A) is a two-plane contained in U and cannot lie in any point line; its linear coefficient sections span H0(O_C(1)). Thus h0(E|C(-3))=1 and h0(E|C(-2))=6. With global generation of E and E^vee(1) as assumed from Denham–Miro-Roig–Schenck and c1(E)=5, all nine splitting degrees lie in [0,3] and sum to 15; their h0 counts force (3,2^4,1^4). Isotropy of two-plane A is one smooth symplectic Plucker hyperplane equation in Gr(2,6), giving the seven-dimensional jumping divisor. I inspected the actual RESULT.md and verify.py; the reported fifteen coordinate-plane checks are consistent but do not establish universality. Boundary: smooth cubics over C and this symplectic bundle only.
